source_text: Τίνα δὲ δοκεῖτε τύπον εἶναι, ὅτι ἐντέταλται τῷ Ἰσραὴλ προσφέρειν δάμαλιν τοὺς ἄνδρας, ἐν οἷς εἰσὶν ἁμαρτίαι τέλειαι, καὶ σφάξαντας κατακαίειν, καὶ αἴρειν τότε τὴν σποδὸν παιδία καὶ βάλλειν εἰς ἄγγη καὶ περιτιθέναι τὸ ἔριον τὸ κόκκινον ἐπὶ ξύλον ʽἴδε πάλιν ὁ τύπος ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ τὸ ἔριον τὸ κόκκινον̓ καὶ τὸ ὕσσωπον, καὶ οὕτως ῥαντίζειν τὰ παιδία καθ̓ ἕνα τὸν λαόν, ἵνα ἁγνίζωνται ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν; νοεῖτε, πῶς ἐν ἁπλότητι λέγει ὑμῖν. ὁ μόσχος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐστίν, οἱ προσφέροντες ἄνδρες ἁμαρτωλοὶ οἱ προσενέγκαντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὴν σφαγήν. εἶτα οὐκέτι ἄνδρες, οὐκέτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ἡ δόξα. οἱ ῥαντίζοντες παῖδες οἱ εὐαγγελισάμενοι ἡμῖν τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ τὸν ἁγνισμὸν τῆς καρδίας, οἷς ἔδωκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τὴν ἐξουσίαν ʽοὖσιν δεκάδυο εἰς μαρτύριον τῶν φυλῶν ὅτι δεκάδυο φυλαὶ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ’ , εἰς τὸ κηρύσσειν. διὰ τί δὲ τρεῖς παῖδες οἱ ῥαντίζοντες; εἰς μαρτύριον Ἀβραάμ, Ἰσαάκ, Ἰακώβ, ὅτι οὗτοι μεγάλοι τῷ θεῷ. ὅτι δὲ τὸ ἔριον ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον ; ὅτι ἡ βασιλεία Ἰησοῦ ἐπὶ ξύλου, καὶ ὅτι οἱ ἐλπίζοντες ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ζήσονται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. διὰ τί δὲ ἅμα τὸ ἔριον καὶ τὸ ὕσσωπον; ὅτι ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ ἡμέραι ἔσονται πονηραὶ καὶ ῥυπαραί, ἐν αἷς ἡμεῖς σωθησόμεθα: ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἀλγῶν σάρκα διὰ τοῦ ῥύπου τοῦ ὑσσύπου ἰᾶται. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὕτως γενόμενα ἡμῖν μέν ἐστιν φανερά, ἐκείνοις δὲ σκοτεινά, ὅτι οὐκ ἤκουσαν φωνῆς κυρίου.
pass_a_gloss: What do you think the type is, that it was commanded to Israel to offer a heifer, the men in whom are complete sins, and having slaughtered to burn, and to take then the ashes and throw into a vessel and to put the red wool on wood? Behold again the type of the cross and the red wool and the hyssop, and thus to sprinkle the children one by one the people, so that they may be purified from the sins? Understand how in simplicity He speaks to you. The calf is Jesus, the men offering sinful who brought Him to the slaughter. Then no longer men, no longer of sinners the glory. The sprinkling children the ones who evangelized to us the forgiveness of the sins and the purification of the heart, to whom He gave the authority of the gospel, being twelve for testimony of the tribes, that twelve tribes of Israel, for preaching. Why then three children the sprinkling? For testimony of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, because these are great to God. And why the wool on the wood? Because the kingdom of Jesus is on wood, and because those hoping in Him will live to the age. Why then both the wool and the hyssop? Because in His kingdom there will be evil and filthy days, in which we will be saved: because also the one suffering flesh through the filth of the hyssop heals. And because of this thus having happened it is clear to us, but to them dark, because they did not hear the voice of the Lord.
pass_b_english: What do you suppose the pattern means? God commanded Israel to offer a heifer, but the men who do so are people in whom sin has reached its full measure. After they slaughter and burn it, they take the ashes and throw them into a vessel, then put the red wool on wood — here again is the pattern of the cross, the red wool, and the hyssop — and so they sprinkle the children, one by one, the whole people, so that they may be purified from their sins (Numbers 19:1-10). Understand how simply He speaks to you. The heifer is Jesus. The men who offer it are the sinners who handed Him over for slaughter. After that there are no longer men; the glory of sinners is gone. The children who do the sprinkling are the ones who evangelized us with the forgiveness of sins and the purification of the heart, to whom He gave the authority of the gospel. There are twelve of them, for a testimony to the tribes — because there are twelve tribes of Israel — so that they might preach. Why are there three children who sprinkle? As a testimony to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because these men are great before God. And why is the wool placed on the wood? Because the kingdom of Jesus is on the wood, and because those who hope in Him will live forever. Why both the wool and the hyssop? Because in His kingdom there will be evil and filthy days, in which we will be saved: for even the one who suffers in the flesh is healed through the filth of the hyssop. And because of this, what has happened this way is clear to us, but dark to them, because they did not hear the voice of the Lord.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass B correctly identifies the ritual described as the red heifer ritual and provides the appropriate scripture citation (Numbers 19:1-10) for the content described in the Greek. All clauses, including the theological interpretations of the symbols (the calf/heifer as Jesus, the wood as the cross, etc.), are preserved in both Pass A and Pass B.
